title: incident-bot: oncall autodiagnostics helpers & SLO toolkit integration
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve on-call diagnostics workflow by exposing compact helper suggestions from incident-bot and wiring the SLO toolkit utilities into the autodiagnostics pipeline. This PR adds a small API adapter, new helper rules that surface runbook quicklinks and suggested checks, and end-to-end telemetry hooks so on-call can triage faster.

What this changes: added a lightweight SLO toolkit adapter to translate SLO metadata into incident-bot helper suggestions; implemented a set of 'oncall helper' heuristics that synthesize likely runbook steps and relevant traces/metrics links; surfaced compact runbook snippets in the Slack on-call message; added unit/integration tests and docs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add SLO toolkit adapter and helper rules
- [x] Add unit + integration tests covering primary heuristics
- [x] Add telemetry metrics for helper click-through and suggestion accuracy
- [x] Update docs with runbook examples and troubleshooting
- [x] Validate rate-limiting and fallback behavior

Notes: Keeps the helpers additive (no behavioural change to existing autodiagnostics unless enabled via feature flag incident_bot.autodiag_helpers_enabled). This PR is focused on production-ready ergonomics: observability, perf (minimal overhead path), and safe fallbacks if SLO toolkit lookup times out.

perf: cache SLO metadata lookups for 30s to reduce downstream calls

ci_checks: integration-tests: flaky first run (timeout on slo lookup) -> re-run -> pass
discussion: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Nice direction. Two asks: (1) add a circuit breaker for SLO toolkit calls so we don't slow autodiag; (2) can we limit snippet length to 300 chars in Slack attachments?
Maya Chen (author): Added circuit-breaker with 250ms timeout + local 30s cache; truncated snippets to 280 chars and added a 'view more' link to runbook page.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Can you add a metric for helper suggestion accuracy (clicked vs suggested) so we can iterate?
Maya Chen (author): Added telemetry counter incident_bot.helper_suggestion_clicked and instrumented replies; included in observability/metrics/incident_bot.yaml.
Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Tests look good. Minor nit: prefer exponential backoff in slo_toolkit_adapter for transient 5xxs
Maya Chen (author): Switched to small exp backoff (50ms, 100ms) and added comment explaining bounds to avoid blowing up request latency.
Sofia Martins: Approved and verified docs. (approve)
merge: merged via squash by Maya Chen. Squash commit message: 'feat(incident-bot): oncall autodiagnostics helpers + slo-toolkit adapter — add helper rules, telemetry, tests, and docs'
release_notes: Incident-bot: adds opt-in oncall autodiagnostics helpers that surface runbook quicklinks, SLO context, and suggested triage steps. Feature is off by default; enable via feature flag incident_bot.autodiag_helpers_enabled. Includes observability for suggestion clicks and accuracy metrics.
notes_for_backport: Small surface area change; backport to release/1.14 if teams want the feature earlier. Ensure the slo-toolkit client version is >= 0.9.2 due to adapter call signature.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: SLO toolkit lookup could add latency to autodiag flow. Mitigation: 250ms circuit-breaker, short cache, safe fallback that keeps current autodiag behavior. Tests included for timeouts and fallbacks.
manual_steps_to_validate: 1) Enable feature flag incident_bot.autodiag_helpers_enabled in staging. 2) Trigger a synthetic SLO alert using SRE-112 test harness. 3) Verify Slack message contains runbook quicklink and compact snippet. 4) Verify metrics incident_bot.helper_suggestion_clicked increments on click.
